The Bipartisan Premium Tax Credit Extension Act (H.R. 5145) proves Washington’s addiction to temporary subsidies over real healthcare reform. While premiums could spike 21% if credits expire, the core issue remains: D.C. props up a broken system instead of crushing hospital monopolies and Big Pharma price-gouging.

KFF data shows 80,000 Washingtonians might drop coverage – not because subsidies end, but because bureaucrats refuse to tackle medical cartels inflating costs. Every dollar spent on this subsidy band-aid could instead fund permanent price transparency laws and competitive insurance markets.

Until Congress stops feeding the beast with taxpayer-funded patches, premiums will keep bleeding Americans dry.

The real issue isn’t tax credits—it’s the ACA’s structural failures that let Big Pharma and insurance middlemen jack up prices while bureaucrats pocket the difference. Premiums are soaring because the system prioritizes corporate profits over patients.

The Big Beautiful Bill tackles this by expanding Health Savings Accounts and unleashing catastrophic coverage options that bypass bloated bureaucracy. Instead of throwing more taxpayer cash at a broken model, let’s force transparency in drug pricing and break monopolies.

When hospitals charge $50 for a Tylenol and insurers take 20% off the top, no subsidy can fix that rot. Real reform means market-driven care, not perpetual bailouts for a rigged system.

Snohomish County’s $114M “Housing & Behavioral Health Capital Fund” is textbook bureaucratic bloat. $3M for workshops and grant applications? Classic D.C. math—burn cash on compliance theater while actual healthcare access stagnates.

Instead of funneling millions into administrative black holes, slash the red tape and let private providers deliver care efficiently.

Taxpayers fund solutions, not endless government middlemen.
